newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Informix busy as stock rallies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Informix busy as stock rallies.

text.p: Options on shares of Informix Corp were relatively busy Thursday as the stock rose on heavy turnover, traders said.
"It's up on takeover rumors," an options trader in Chicago said of Informix shares, which gained 2-3/16 to close at 11-3/8, just off their 11-1/2 session high.
Traders said the takeover talk was vague, with no suitors' names emerging. Analysts said possible buyers could include Computer Associates International Inc or Netscape Communications Corp.
A spokesman for the database software company declined to comment on the takeover speculation.
The trader in Chicago said Informix options activity was two-way, with buyers and sellers active.
"It's really a mixture," he said. "There's a lot more buy pressure in the options, but there's also people selling."
He added that options volume began to increase on Wednesday but ballooned on Thursday.
Most Informix options crossed on the Chicago Board Options Exchange. The options also trade at the American Stock Exchange.
"For the most part there's been decent activity in the options," the head of one options trading desk said. "We've mostly had people speculating on the long side."
The Informix June 10 calls were most active, with total turnover of roughly 3,800. The May 10 calls traded 3,345.
Other busy calls included the June 12-1/2s, the August 10s and the August 12-1/2s.
On the put side, the May 10 traded 1,505 contracts and the June 10 traded 1,020.
Volatilities in the June series ranged from the mid-80 region to the mid-90s, up from a historic volatility of around 70.
"Volatilities have gone up a little bit but they're not jumping a lot," the trader in Chicago said. "There's definitely a mixture of paper."
Traders said the stock's ability to hold above the 10 level would be key for the near term.
In late March, the shares gapped down to about the 10 level from the 15 zone and eventually bottomed at 6-9/16 on April 28 before working their way back.
